sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Modron, also called Madrun, is a Welsh goddess. Her name means mother. The Mabinogion, the set of Welsh mythic tales, shows her as a mother goddess. She runs parallel to the Deae Matres of the Continent, the divine mothers, and to Matrona, whose name also means mother. Little myth is attached to her. Some scholars view her as an early, even pre-Celtic, deity. In Cornwall a saint Madrun is known, a Christian form of the older goddess. Rituals at the saint's well drop pins into the water to foresee the health of the one who asks. The hero Mabon appears in the tale as her son.
objective: Document Modron, the Welsh mother goddess.
